faq.heading: What is What Was I Doing?
faq.content: A Windows time tracker you start and stop yourself. It records activities, projects, and reports. It does not take screenshots, read keystrokes, or watch which apps you use.

faq.heading: Do I need an account or the internet?
faq.content: No account. Tracking works offline. A connection is only used when you check for an update.

faq.heading: Where is my data stored?
faq.content: Under %LOCALAPPDATA%\WID\ on this PC: activities, projects, categories, and settings. The app also keeps about two weeks of daily backup copies. Uninstalling the program does not delete that folder.

faq.heading: How do I log time?
faq.content: Start activity, pick a category, and add a project or description if you want. The timer starts immediately. Stop activity ends it. If you forgot to start, add a manual entry for the past period.

faq.heading: What do the reports mean?
faq.content: Reports show daily and weekly totals. Unallocated time is your available working hours minus what you tracked. It is only a gap in the log, not a judgement. Lunch is taken out of available hours and is not an activity unless you record it.

faq.heading: What happens at the end of the day?
faq.content: At 17:00, if something is still running, WID asks if you are still working. No answer within 60 seconds stops it and caps that entry at 16:30. On the next start, older sessions that ran past 17:00 are capped the same way.

faq.heading: How do I update or move my data?
faq.content: Help, then Check for updates, compares the build number. Installing a newer zip does not replace your tracked data. File, Export and File, Import move the JSON files if you want a copy.
